system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** §2(d) is the only ownership provision and covers only TrueLink's rights in the Interface. Nothing affirms that we retain rights in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or the borrower/loan data flowing through the Interface (Client Content ownership appears only in §13, on discontinuation of hosting). The results of the Support Services — the programming customization we pay for — are addressed only as confidential/Client Proprietary Information (§§10(b), 10(c)), which is not ownership or a licence.
- **Aggravating factor:** §8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to "use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit" Credit Data. That is a licence rather than an assignment (so not walk-away territory), and it is a negotiated bargain limited by the Credit Data definition and the Non-Competition Agreement, so I left it intact and expressly preserved it in the redline.
- **Why not compliant at fallback:** the fallback requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables; here there is neither ownership nor any surviving licence to paid-for work product, and no data ownership anchor.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a single inserted §2(e) confirming Client ownership of content, IP and data, assignment of Support Services results, TrueLink's retained Interface IP with a perpetual licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, and no joint ownership — with the fallback offered in the comment.

input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination fee on the Client. input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or verification right over Client's usage, records or systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify" and "monitor" return nothing, and the two candidate sections confirm this: Compensation (§ 5/6) runs the wrong way for the vendor — Client is entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges (p0047) — and the Client covenants in § 8 impose compliance and access-restriction duties without any TrueLink right to examine Client's premises, records or systems. Section 2(e) likewise gives Client, not TrueLink, access to usage statistics and raw log files (p0037). The only vendor self-help right is § 8(f), under which TrueLink may "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming or illegal activity (p0058); that operates within TrueLink's own hosted Interface environment and is neither a usage/records audit nor access to Client systems, so it does not engage the walk-away trigger. With no audit obligation binding us, the rule's protective parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, no system access) cannot be exceeded, so the position is better than preferred. We should not insert an audit right the vendor has not asked for, as that would create an obligation against our own party; we simply resist any audit language added in later drafts unless it meets the once-per-12-months / 30 days' notice / independent auditor / vendor-cost standard.

Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or verification right over Client's usage, records or systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify" and "monitor" return nothing, and the two candidate sections confirm this: Compensation (§ 5/6) runs the wrong way for the vendor — Client is entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges (p0047) — and the Client covenants in § 8 impose compliance and access-restriction duties without any TrueLink right to examine Client's premises, records or systems. Section 2(e) likewise gives Client, not TrueLink, access to usage statistics and raw log files (p0037). The only vendor self-help right is § 8(f), under which TrueLink may "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming or illegal activity (p0058); that operates within TrueLink's own hosted Interface environment and is neither a usage/records audit nor access to Client systems, so it does not engage the walk-away trigger. With no audit obligation binding us, the rule's protective parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, no system access) cannot be exceeded, so the position is better than preferred. We should not insert an audit right the vendor has not asked for, as that would create an obligation against our own party; we simply resist any audit language added in later drafts unless it meets the once-per-12-months / 30 days' notice / independent auditor / vendor-cost standard.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

We therefore insert a new Section 31 at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), placed after Section 30 as the last substantive miscellaneous clause, with the fallback limits offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry CGL, E&O and cyber liability insurance and provide certificates on request.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data, so we have added our standard requirement (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). If helpful, we can accept reduced limits of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (c) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering TrueLink's hosting of the Web Site and processing of Client Content and other data; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. TrueLink shall provide Client with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

paragraphs.text: 10. CONFIDENTIALITY.

a. Client acknowledges its responsibility to preserve the confidentiality of certain technology, information, and documentation embedded in the Interface and agrees to respect the confidential nature of the Interface. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, it is understood and agreed that Client's confidentiality obligations relating to any System and any data, documentation, or other output from such System shall include those specified in any agreements between Client and the licensor of the System.

b. TrueLink acknowledges its responsibilities to preserve the confidentiality of all results of the Support Services, Client's Intellectual Property, and subject to Section 8(d) herein Client Confidential Information.

c. The parties hereto recognize that certain of the information and documentation previously provided or that may in the future be provided by a party to the other related to the matters covered by this Agreement includes privileged, confidential and proprietary information belonging to such party (a party's "Proprietary Information") which, if disclosed, could result in substantial and irreparable harm to such party. For information and documentation to qualify as a party's Proprietary Information, such information must either be marked "Confidential" or otherwise identified in writing as confidential at or prior to the time of its delivery to the other hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will automatically be deemed TrueLink Proprietary Information, whether or not specifically marked or designated as such:

(i) any implementation information or user's guides for the Interface, (ii) any advance releases of TrueLink promotional material, (iii) information concerning TrueLink's business plans and strategies, and (iv) TrueLink's customer list. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will be automatically deemed Client Proprietary Information: Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services, including any information or materials of any type or nature, tangible or intangible, disclosed by Client as a result of the TrueLink's relationship with Client relating to the business, products or technology or potential business, products or technology of Client, business plans, financial information, borrower and loan data technical specifications, design concepts,

-6- 7 technical information, customer lists, pricing information, marketing plans and other similar information pertaining to Client. Each agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials as strictly confidential, except to the extent otherwise agreed by the other in writing. Except to the extent otherwise agreed by both parties in writing, party further agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials which it prepares using or based on the other's Proprietary information or any portion thereof (the "Derivative Documentation") as strictly confidential, including, without limitation, any notes made and all reports prepared in connection with this Agreement.

d. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the restrictions on disclosure and other obligations set forth above with respect to Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation shall not apply when, and to the extent that such Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public through no fault of the receiving party; (ii) was previously known to the receiving party free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iii) is subsequently disclosed to the receiving party by a third party who may transfer and disclose such information without restriction and free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iv) is independently developed by the receiving party or a third party without reference to or any use of the

disclosing party's proprietary information; or (v) is required to be disclosed by the receiving party as a matter of law, provided that the receiving party uses all reasonable efforts to provide the disclosing party with at least ten days' prior notice of such disclosure.

11. STANDARD OF CARE. TrueLink shall perform the Hosting and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services for Client with the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (licensor/host).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (licensor/host).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Kind: parametric

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:

**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement contains no audit right running against us. I checked both planner candidates and swept the full document for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify", "monitor" and "usage":

- **§ 5/6 Compensation (p0047)** — verification runs in our favour only: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges, and we may contest them. No vendor right to examine our records.
- **§ 8 Client covenants** — imposes compliance-with-laws, access-restriction and content warranties, but no inspection or examination right.
- **§ 2(e) (p0037)** — usage statistics and raw log files flow *to* Client, not the reverse.
- **§ 8(f) (p0058)** — the only vendor self-help right ("technical mechanisms" against spamming) operates inside TrueLink's own hosted Interface, so it is neither a usage/records audit nor remote access to Client systems; the walk-away trigger is not engaged.

Because no audit obligation binds us, the rule's parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) cannot be breached — the position sits better than preferred. Inserting an audit clause would manufacture an obligation against our own party, so no edit is warranted. Watch-item for later drafts: if TrueLink adds audit or verification language, hold it to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems (fallback: annual, 15 days' notice, 10% cost-shift threshold).

**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

- **§5 Compensation (p0045, p0047):** only ordinary fees for requested Hosting/Support Services, invoiced monthly and payable within 15 days. No late-payment penalty, no fixed or stipulated damages. The blank minimum monthly amounts are in-term fees, not a termination payout.
- **§7 Unsolicited Commercial E-mail (p0049):** a behavioural covenant only — no per-message charge or penalty chargeable to Client.
- **§13/§14 Term and Termination (p0078, p0079):** Client may elect to terminate with services (and fees) simply running to the last day of the following month; there is no early-termination fee, minimum payout, or remaining-contract-value liability.

No Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties exist anywhere in the document, which sits at the playbook's **preferred** position, so no redline was proposed. Worth completing commercially (not a deviation): the blank minimum monthly fee figures in §5a, which §6 also carves out of Client's right to contest charges.

**Finding: missing — insurance obligation absent (severity: low).**

- A full-text search for "insurance" returned nothing, and the miscellaneous run (Sections 13–30), Client covenants (sec-8) and indemnity (sec-12) contain no coverage requirement.
- TrueLink hosts the Client's Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data via the Interface, so this is squarely a vendor that should carry coverage — the absence sits in walk-away territory, and the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is also unmet.
- Redline validated (`ok:true`) and submitted: new Section 31 inserted after Section 30 (Force Majeure) at the preferred limits — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, surviving one year post-term.
- Noted for negotiation, not flagged: the survival clause in Section 25 (p0090) refers to "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so if TrueLink accepts the new section we should conform that cross-reference to "through 31"; the clause's own one-year tail covers the point in the interim. The comment also offers the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if TrueLink pushes back.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

input.quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
input.rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty; there is no warranty that the Interface or related software conforms to its documentation, no malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's standard of care requires only the care TrueLink "customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard, not industry standard, and it carries no warranty remedy. The disclaimer at p0076 is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow express warranties and needs no carve-out; the problem is that there is no express performance warranty to preserve. This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so we insert the playbook performance warranty at the preferred position (12-month conformance, professional and workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws, repair/replace/refund at TrueLink's option), flagging a 90-day period as an acceptable fallback.

If TrueLink prefers, we can work with a ninety (90) day conformance period.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (licensor/host).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
input.rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty; there is no warranty that the Interface or related software conforms to its documentation, no malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's standard of care requires only the care TrueLink "customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard, not industry standard, and it carries no warranty remedy. The disclaimer at p0076 is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow express warranties and needs no carve-out; the problem is that there is no express performance warranty to preserve. This fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so we insert the playbook performance warranty at the preferred position (12-month conformance, professional and workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws, repair/replace/refund at TrueLink's option), flagging a 90-day period as an acceptable fallback.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I found:

- **§ 9 "TrueLink Warranties" (p0059–p0060)** is TrueLink's only express warranty, and it is limited to Y2K date processing. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no malicious-code warranty, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no warranty remedy.
- **§ 11 "Standard of Care" (p0069)** requires only "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard rather than an industry standard, and it attaches no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy.
- **The disclaimer (p0076)** is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does **not** swallow express warranties — no carve-out needed. This is not a walk-away "AS IS" clause; the gap is simply that there is no express performance warranty to preserve.

Because the agreement lacks both a conformance period and any remedy, it fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.

Redline (inserted after p0060, preferred position): TrueLink warrants (a) professional and workmanlike performance of Hosting, Support and other services consistent with industry standards; (b) 12-month conformance of the Interface and related software to documentation and specifications; (c) freedom from malicious code; and (d) compliance with applicable laws — with Client's remedy being re-performance, repair/replacement, or refund of fees paid, at TrueLink's option. The comment offers a 90-day conformance period as the fallback if TrueLink pushes back.
Let me check Sections 3 and 4 (referenced by the termination clause and the minimum fee reference).

a. Storage. ___ megabytes (MB) of disk space on TrueLink's servers will be used for storage of the Web Site and any data files associated with the Web Site.

b. Response Time. TrueLink agrees to use reasonable commercial efforts, consistent with efforts provided to its other Clients to ensure reasonable response times for users accessing the Web Site. Reasonable response times shall be measured as follows: at a mutually agreed to time Client will conduct three tests of the time that it takes to load the home page of the Web Site from an IBM compatible computer (with a 16550 UART chip and an Intel 80586 300 MHZ processor running Windows 98 or NT and Microsoft Internet Explorer (with the cache turned off) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem (the results of these tests will be reported to TrueLink upon completion); reasonable response times means that at all times the time it takes to load the home page of the Web Site using a properly configured IBM compatible computer (as set forth above) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem shall in no event exceed twice the average of the three test response times.

c. Bandwidth. ___ MB of monthly bandwidth (data transfer). In the event that the response time is not reasonable as determined under section 3.1 hereof, upon written notice from Client, TrueLink will, within a reasonable period of time, use reasonable commercial efforts to increase the bandwidth as necessary to make the response time reasonable.

d. Availability. The Web Site will be available Client's to Internet users approximately 24 hours a day, seven days a week, normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted. To minimize server downtime during peak usage periods,

the same location as TrueLink's server.
g. Internet Connection. TrueLink will maintain redundant connections to the Internet on diverse backbones.

h. Domain Names. TrueLink shall provide assistance to Client in securing one or more domain names, sub-domain names or URL's associated therewith; provided that prior to TrueLink providing such assistance, Client shall engage in an appropriate trademark search reasonably satisfactory to TrueLink in order to establish that no domain name proposed by Client shall infringe upon the trademark, service mark, name, or logo of any third party. i. Credit Bureau Information. Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface. TrueLink makes no representation or warranty, and shall have no liability for the truth or completeness of any data so transmitted.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. (Client); counterparty is TrueLink, Inc. (licensor/host).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

I have what I need. Let me confirm the key analysis before submitting.

**Analysis:**

1. **The only Customer-side minimum** is in §5(a) (p0045): fees "not less than $\_\_\_\_ per month for the Hosting Services and $\_\_\_\_ per month for Support Services" — a monthly floor, not an annual volume commitment.
2. **Term** (p0078): 1 year, auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal — so no multi-year lock-in.
3. **Exit** (p0079, §14): Client may elect to terminate at any time by written notice, with services (and therefore the monthly minimums) running only to the last day of the following month — an at-will exit on roughly 30 days' notice.
4. **No shortfall/penalty mechanic** anywhere: no acceleration, no take-or-pay true-up penalty, and §2(a) (p0022) confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License."

This is a commitment capped at the current 12-month term, terminable on ~30 days' notice, with no shortfall penalty — squarely the fallback position, so no redline.

input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: The only minimum commitment imposed on Client is the monthly fee floor in § 5(a) (p0045) for Hosting and Support Services. That commitment sits at our fallback position rather than the preferred usage-only position, and is therefore acceptable without redline: (i) it is bounded by a one-year term that auto-renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to stop renewal on 30 days' notice (p0078); (ii) Client has a standalone at-will exit under § 14, where services — and hence the monthly minimums — run only to the last day of the month following Client's termination notice (p0079), i.e. roughly a 30-day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere in the document, and § 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License" (p0022). No multi-year take-or-pay or volume cap on Client usage exists, so walk-away territory is not engaged. Two minor points noted but not flagged as deviations: the § 14 exit is stated as "Subject to Section 4," and § 4 is TrueLink's own commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than ____ months," which could be argued to hold the Support Services minimum open past termination — the blank is unfilled and § 4 reads as a vendor-side obligation benefiting us, so we would clarify only if that blank is completed with a long period. Separately, § 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights, which is a billing-transparency point for the audit/disputes rule rather than a minimum-commitment failure. The requirement in § 3(i) (p0042) that Client order a credit report per underwriting approval is a requirements/exclusivity term addressed under that rule, not double-flagged here.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

I have what I need. Let me confirm the key analysis before submitting.

**Analysis:**

1. **The only Customer-side minimum** is in §5(a) (p0045): fees "not less than $\_\_\_\_ per month for the Hosting Services and $\_\_\_\_ per month for Support Services" — a monthly floor, not an annual volume commitment.
2. **Term** (p0078): 1 year, auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal — so no multi-year lock-in.
3. **Exit** (p0079, §14): Client may elect to terminate at any time by written notice, with services (and therefore the monthly minimums) running only to the last day of the following month — an at-will exit on roughly 30 days' notice.
4. **No shortfall/penalty mechanic** anywhere: no acceleration, no take-or-pay true-up penalty, and §2(a) (p0022) confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License."

This is a commitment capped at the current 12-month term, terminable on ~30 days' notice, with no shortfall penalty — squarely the fallback position, so no redline.

input.rationale: The only minimum commitment imposed on Client is the monthly fee floor in § 5(a) (p0045) for Hosting and Support Services. That commitment sits at our fallback position rather than the preferred usage-only position, and is therefore acceptable without redline: (i) it is bounded by a one-year term that auto-renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to stop renewal on 30 days' notice (p0078); (ii) Client has a standalone at-will exit under § 14, where services — and hence the monthly minimums — run only to the last day of the month following Client's termination notice (p0079), i.e. roughly a 30-day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere in the document, and § 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License" (p0022). No multi-year take-or-pay or volume cap on Client usage exists, so walk-away territory is not engaged. Two minor points noted but not flagged as deviations: the § 14 exit is stated as "Subject to Section 4," and § 4 is TrueLink's own commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than ____ months," which could be argued to hold the Support Services minimum open past termination — the blank is unfilled and § 4 reads as a vendor-side obligation benefiting us, so we would clarify only if that blank is completed with a long period. Separately, § 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights, which is a billing-transparency point for the audit/disputes rule rather than a minimum-commitment failure. The requirement in § 3(i) (p0042) that Client order a credit report per underwriting approval is a requirements/exclusivity term addressed under that rule, not double-flagged here.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (at fallback)** — no redline proposed.

The agreement does impose a Customer-side minimum (the monthly fee floors in § 5(a)), so this is not the preferred "usage only" position. But it clears the fallback on every material term:

| Fallback requirement | Document |
|---|---|
| Commitment limited to current 12-month term | § 13 (p0078): 1-year term, auto-renew in one-year increments, 30-day non-renewal notice |
| Reducible/exitable on 30 days' notice | § 14 (p0079): Client's at-will termination; fees stop the last day of the month following notice |
| True-up rather than penalty | No shortfall, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere; § 2(a) confirms Client is not obligated to use the License |

Since a clause at the fallback is acceptable and not redlined, I left § 5(a) untouched.

Two items I noted in the rationale rather than flagging:
- **§ 14's "Subject to Section 4"** — § 4 is TrueLink's commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than \_\_\_\_ months." That blank could theoretically be filled with a long period and argued to keep the Support Services minimum alive past termination. Worth watching at signature, but as drafted it is a vendor-side obligation running in our favour.
- **§ 6 (p0047)** carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and challenge rights — a billing-transparency issue belonging to the audit/disputes rule.

I also declined to double-flag § 3(i) (p0042), which requires Client to order a credit report per underwriting approval; that is a requirements/exclusivity term, not a minimum-volume commitment with a shortfall consequence.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and Credit Data, but no exit provision exists. Section 13 only confirms that Client retains ownership of its domains and Client Content and makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment within 30/60 days; Section 14 merely continues services until the end of the month following notice. That falls short of even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition/data-return paragraph in the termination section, noting the 90-day fallback in the comment.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and Credit Data, but no exit provision exists. Section 13 only confirms that Client retains ownership of its domains and Client Content and makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment within 30/60 days; Section 14 merely continues services until the end of the month following notice. Neither obliges TrueLink to provide transition assistance, to return or export our data in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion afterwards, and Section 10 contains no return-of-materials mechanic. That falls short of even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition/data-return paragraph in the termination section, noting the 90-day fallback in the comment.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium severity) — TRANSITION**

The agreement has no exit/transition provision:

- **§13 (p0078)** only confirms Client retains ownership of its domains and Client Content, and puts the burden *on us* to arrange a new name server (30 days) / hosting environment (60 days).
- **§14 (p0079)** just continues services until the last day of the month following our termination notice.
- **§10 (Confidentiality)** contains no return-of-materials or deletion mechanic, and nothing elsewhere addresses data export.

Since TrueLink hosts our Client Content and Credit Data, this fails even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days). I inserted the preferred clause as new §14a immediately after the termination paragraph (which sits within the surviving Sections 5–30): up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of all Client Content/Credit Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and deletion with written certification thereafter — with the 90-day fallback offered in the negotiation comment. Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

That fails even the fallback, which requires a vendor IP indemnity, while Client's indemnity in § 12(a) is broad (Client breach, Web Site/Client Content, and injury or damage from anything transmitted from the Web Site). We therefore inserted a new § 12(c) giving the preferred vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content/Credit Data and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and Client Content and Client-modification carve-outs. We have left § 12(a) as drafted rather than narrowing it, keeping the edit minimal.","proposal":"Add TrueLink IP infringement / misconduct indemnity with standard defence procedure","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-ip-21bdfe5f","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The only ownership provision (§2(d)) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface and says nothing about our side of the line. There is no affirmative statement that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or the borrower/loan data transmitted through the Interface (Client Content ownership is acknowledged only on discontinuation of hosting, in §13), and no ownership or licence provision for the results of the Support Services (i.e., the programming customization work we pay for) — §§10(b) and 10(c) treat those results only as confidential/Client Proprietary Information, which is not ownership. Combined with §8(d), under which Client grants TrueLink a worldwide licence to \"use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit\" Credit Data, the agreement leaves our data and paid-for work product without any ownership anchor, failing the fallback (which at minimum requires a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the deliverables) on a material term. We therefore inserted a minimal ownership clause: Client retains all rights in its content, IP and data (expressly preserving the existing §8(d) Credit Data licence bargain), Support Services results are assigned to Client with a perpetual licence back for any embedded TrueLink IP, TrueLink's Interface ownership is preserved, and no joint ownership is created.","proposal":"Add Client ownership of Client Content, data and Support Services work product, with licence back of embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership.","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-6a63cb36","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, buried in the indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink's liability at 12 months' hosting/support compensation, while Client's liability — including under the very broad indemnity in Section 12(a) (p0071-p0072) covering any breach, Web Site/Client Content claims and third-party injury — is entirely uncapped. There is also no defined set of carve-outs (only TrueLink's own gross negligence/wilful misconduct is excepted) and no confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. Our redline makes the cap mutual and agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' fees and US$1,000,000 and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence. We have not added a mutual consequential-damages waiver (absent from the document), as its absence preserves our recovery against the vendor; that is noted rather than redlined.","proposal":"Make the cap mutual and agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' fees or US$1,000,000, with standard uncapped carve-outs.","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision (no change-of-control language appears anywhere, so TrueLink has no CoC termination or re-pricing right — that limb is satisfied). However, the clause requires the other party's prior written approval with no reasonableness standard and, critically, no carve-out for assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; only a \"financially responsible affiliate\" carve-out exists. That fails the fallback on both material terms (successor assignment on notice, and consent not unreasonably withheld) and leaves TrueLink able to block our M&A or reorganisation. No multi-year take-or-pay or volume cap on Client usage exists, so walk-away territory is not engaged. Separately, § 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights, which is a billing-transparency point for the audit/disputes rule rather than a minimum-commitment failure. Full reads of the two likely host sections — § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) and § 10 (Confidentiality) — confirm Client's only covenants are compliance with laws, non-representation as to underwriting decisions, limiting Interface access, the Credit Data license, content warranties, and confidentiality. This matches our preferred position (\"No non-solicit on Customer\"), so no redline is warranted; there is no duration, scope, or general-advertising carve-out to negotiate.
